# Convocan a perros y gatos con diagnóstico queratosis actínica y carcinoma de células escamosas cutáneo

## La convocatoria de los investigadores de la Facultad de Ciencias Veterinarias de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata está destinada a pacientes caninos y felinos para participar de un ensayo clínico cuyos objetivos son evaluar aspectos diagnósticos, pronósticos y nuevas alternativas de tratamiento en estas enfermedades.

Foto: FCV-UNLP

Un equipo de investigadores de la Facultad de Ciencias Veterinarias de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata (FCV-UNLP) convoca a pacientes caninos y felinos con lesiones cutáneas pre-malignas -queratosis actínica y/o carcinoma de células escamosas in situ- para participar de un ensayo clínico cuyos objetivos son evaluar aspectos diagnósticos, pronósticos y nuevas alternativas de tratamiento en estas enfermedades.

Esta es una excelente oportunidad para que los tutores de perros y gatos con lesiones cutáneas pre-malignas puedan acceder al diagnóstico y tratamiento de estas lesiones en forma gratuita.

El desarrollo de estas lesiones pre-malignas se relaciona con la exposición crónica al sol en áreas de la piel con poco pelo y poco pigmento, y su presencia se asocia con un mayor riesgo de desarrollo de un tipo de cáncer de piel denominado carcinoma de células escamosas cutáneo.

Para poder participar, los tutores de los animales deberán completar un formulario al que se accede desde aquí y en caso de cumplir con los requerimientos serán contactados para coordinar un turno en el Hospital Escuela.

Este estudio se encuentra en el marco del Proyecto de Investigación “Potencial terapéutico de la vía de señalización mTOR en carcinomas de células escamosas cutáneos en caninos y felinos” dirigido por la Doctora Liyare Sanz Ressel, investigadora del Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET) en la FCV-UNLP.

##### Fuente: FCV-UNLP

Faculdade de Medicina Veterinária e Zootecnia da USP

Cães com câncer na região anal podem ajudar na busca do câncer em animais e humanos

Se você possui um cão com câncer anal e que ainda não recebeu nenhum tratamento, ele pode ajudar a Faculdade de Medicina Veterinária e Zootecnia (FMVZ) da USP na investigação sobre cura de câncer em animais e humanos. A pesquisa, que é conduzida pela doutoranda Karina D’Angelo Campos, tem como orientadora a professora Denise Tabacchi Fantoni e está sendo desenvolvida no Departamento de Cirurgia (VCI).

O objetivo do estudo é  avaliar tumores perianais em cães e os efeitos de diferentes medicamentos anestésicos e analgésicos sobre a recuperação pós-cirúrgica e o sistema imunológico, além de investigar se existe correlação entre esses aspectos e o prognóstico da doença.

Podem participar cães de todas raças, gêneros e idades, desde que apresentem câncer suspeito ou confirmado na região anal (nódulo ou massa próximo ao ânus) e que ainda não tenham recebido tratamento. Devem ter comportamento dócil, ou não muito agressivo, e não estejam acometidos de doenças crônicas avançadas como doença cardíaca ou renal, entre outras.

Os proprietários que quiserem incluir seus animais na pesquisa devem entrar em contato com a pesquisadora pelo número (11) 960320242, até o dia 15 de maio, para obter mais informações para avaliação.

## Clinical Trials Now Enrolling

#### CALL FOR PATIENTS: Clinical Trial for Soft Tissue Sarcoma in Dogs

Study Title: Feasibility and dose-optimization clinical trial of local immunotherapy for solid tumors in canine cancer patients

Eligibility: Any dog weighing 5kg or above with at least one cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma lesion that is greater than 1.7cm in diameter is eligible to enroll. All dogs that meet the study criteria will receive the study drug (no placebo) followed by surgical removal of the tumor 1 week later.

Study Purpose: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological effects of a newly designed immunotherapy. Specifically, the study is evaluating the injection of investigational T-cell engagers (TCEs) directly into tumors (intratumorally) in canine patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS). TCEs are engineered antibodies that physically connect T cells to cancer cells by targeting specific markers (CD3 or CD28 on T cells, and B7-H3 or PD-L1 on cancer cells), triggering the immune system to destroy tumor cells.

#### Safety Measures, Risks, and Potential Benefits

While procedures like blood draws, ultrasound, anesthesia, and surgery carry standard medical risks, the investigational TCEs also carry the potential risks of temporary discomfort, minor bleeding, redness, and irritation at the injection site. Although this study seeks to reduce these risks through careful selection of the TCEs and the intratumoral doses to be used, these and other side effects could occur including overactive immune responses/allergic reactions, gastro-intestinal upset, and other potential unforeseen adverse reactions. To mitigate these risks, all enrolled dogs receive pre-treatment diphenhydramine (Benadryl) to reduce allergic reactions, undergo overnight hospital monitoring following injection, and receive carefully adjusted dosages across patient cohorts.

While enrolled dogs may not receive direct health benefits from this trial, their participation will help advance the development of vital cancer treatments for both dogs and humans. Participation in this study will include a $1,500 credit towards surgical removal of the tumor at VRCCO, along with full coverage for any ICU stays, study-related blood work, and medications required due to study participation.

#### For more information on this trial, please contact the Dr. Kristen Couto: [email protected] or click on the button below for more details. 

FOR MORE INFORMATION

Paclitaxel is one of the most effective anticancer agents used in human cancer today, with potent activity against a wide variety of tumors. These studies seek to test whether PaccalVet is safe for use in dogs and cats, and whether it has antitumor activity against certain cancers.

#### What to Expect?

Cats enrolled in the study will receive Paccal Vet via intravenous infusion over 15-30 minutes once every 3 weeks for up to four doses. Throughout those treatment cycles, cats will be monitored carefully for tumor responses and adverse events through physical examinations, blood work, and quality of life questionnaires. Enrollment benefits include all costs associated with treatment as well as diagnostics, including lab work, imaging (x-rays and ultrasound) and examinations during the study.
#### HEMANGIOSARCOMA CLINICAL STUDY

#### Enrollment Now Closed

Veterinary Referral Center of Central Oregon has completed enrollment for dogs with Stage I or II splenic hemangiosarcoma (HSA) that have recently undergone splenectomy. While anti-tumor activity has been documented in other cancers in dogs, studies have not yet been performed in hemangiosarcoma. This study seeks to test whether Paccal Vet is safe for use in dogs with hemangiosarcoma and whether the drug may improve their survival.

#### What to Expect?

Each patient will be actively participating in the study for up to 12 months from the time of splenectomy or until disease progression. Enrolled patients will receive a total of 4 doses of Paccal Vet, administered 3 weeks apart. Enrollment benefits include all costs associated with treatment as well as diagnostics, including lab work, imaging (x-rays and ultrasound) and examinations during the study.

LEARN MORE ABOUT THIS TRIAL

This study has been reviewed and approved by an ethical review board and will be conducted in compliance with VICH-GCP guidelines. It is being run by CASTR Alliance Inc., a veterinary clinical research organization. Enrollment in this study is voluntary.

2026.02.04 18:13

公益財団法人日本小動物医療センター（埼玉県所沢市）では、最先端の免疫療法である抗PD-1抗体を用いた、犬と猫の難治性のがんに対する獣医師主導の臨床試験を実施している。
経済的な理由で治療を諦めていた飼い主の方々へ新たな希望を提供することを目的として、センターの公益事業の一環で、がんに苦しむ犬や猫とその飼い主の方々を支援するため、がん治療に関する診療費の補助を行っているという。
獣医療における新しい治療手段を確立させることを目指す、動物のがん治療の最先端の取り組みをレポートする。

## プロジェクト本文

目標達成の御礼と、最終日までの応援のお願い

日頃より本プロジェクト「子宮体がん再発後も、妊娠の可能性を守るための挑戦。臨床研究の継続へ」に温かいご支援をいただき、誠にありがとうございます。

 

2025年10月16日の開始以来、多くの皆さまにご厚志をお寄せいただきました結果、11月21日にネクストゴールである980万円も達成することができました。みなさまのご協力に対し、心より御礼申し上げます。

 

ご寄付を通じて、「再発後も妊娠の希望を諦めずに治療を続けたい」という患者さんの想いに共感し、私たちの挑戦を支えてくださる方々がこれほど多くいらっしゃることに、研究チーム一同、深く励まされております。

 

本クラウドファンディングは 12月14日（日）23:00 まで 続きます。さらなるネクストゴールは設定いたしませんが、最終日までのご支援は研究推進のため、特に下記のような目的で大切に活用いたします。

 

・ 試験データの統計解析
・ 本研究の国内外学会での発信・発表
・ 研究成果を世界へ届けるための論文作成・投稿

# Ongoing EU Clinical Trials

ESVONC attaches great importance to innovation and evidence-based medicine in the field of veterinary oncology. Therefore, we are happy to share with you with a monthly overview of ongoing canine and feline oncology trials in Europe. We are convinced that knowledge of these trials will enhance collaboration between researchers and clinicians, thus increasing recruitment for clinical trials and treatment options for dogs and cats.
Please find below a non-exhaustive listing of ongoing trials as gathered in the Oncowaf database. For more details about these trials, please visit https://oncowaf.be/en/ClinicalTrials.

If you have an ongoing clinical trial and would like to add it to the Oncowaf clinical trial database and this mailing, please contact contact@oncowaf.com. This list is an intiative of dr. Laetitia Cicchelero (DVM, PhD, Cross-health coordinator @ Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Ghent University). Laetitia is initiator and inspirer of ONCOWAF. ESVONC wishes to thank Laetitia for her efforts to create this useful overview.

This list is updated on a monthly basis.
(green: new trial, orange: trial enters its last month of recruitment).
